content.introduction: The latest data show a 3.4% annual headline inflation rate as of August 2026, with core inflation at 2.4%. However, the September 2026 CPI report, released on October 14, 2026, indicates an increase to 3.7% for the year, driven by higher energy prices. Specifically, gasoline prices rose 34.2% year-over-year, and fuel oil prices increased 74.2%. Shelter inflation also accelerated to 3.2%, while food inflation slowed to 2.5%. The monthly CPI increase was 0.6%, marking its largest gain in five months.
body:
For now, the latest data show a 3.4% annual headline inflation rate, while core inflation stands at 2.4%. Future reports will help show whether price pressures continue at a similar pace or begin moving higher or lower. Consumers, businesses, and policymakers will continue watching categories such as energy, shelter, food, and other services to understand how the inflation picture develops through the remainder of 2026.

FAQs

### Q1. What is the US inflation rate? [...] The August 2026 CPI report was released on September 11, 2026. The next U.S. CPI report, covering September 2026, is scheduled for October 14, 2026, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. [...] For households, an inflation rate of 3.4% means that the overall cost of the goods and services measured by the CPI was higher than it was a year earlier. However, inflation does not affect every category equally. Some prices increased much faster than the overall rate, while others moved only slightly or even declined. This is why individual families may experience a different change in their everyday expenses depending on what they regularly buy.

## What the Latest CPI Data Shows

## The US annual inflation rate accelerated to 3.7% in September 2026, up from 3.4% in each of the previous two months and above market expectations of 3.6%, driven by higher energy prices. Gasoline rose 34.2% yoy, more than 27.4% in August and fuel oil prices increased 74.2%, compared with 52% previously. Inflation also accelerated for shelter, to 3.2% from 3%, but slowed for food to 2.5% from 2.7%.
